findings.evidence:
New format is introduced in `pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go`:
- `TempIndexValueElem.Encode` (deleted+distinct) now conditionally appends `TempIndexKeyTypePartitionIDFlag` ('p') + `codec.EncodeInt(partitionID)` when `TempIndexValueElem.Global` is true.
- `TempIndexValueElem.DecodeOne` (TempIndexValueFlagDeleted) now checks `b[0] == TempIndexKeyTypePartitionIDFlag` and consumes 9 bytes before reading `KeyVer`, wrapping the handle via `kv.NewPartitionHandle(pid, v.Handle)`.
The writer is enabled by DML in `pkg/table/tables/index.go` `(*index).Delete`: when `c.idxInfo.Global` it sets `tempValElem.Global = true` and `tempValElem.Handle = kv.NewPartitionHandle(c.phyTblID, h)`, so upgraded nodes will emit the new bytes.
Forward-compat break: the first-parent decoder (`5da9d1a^1:pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go`) expects `[handle][key_version]` immediately; it has no branch for 'p'. If it reads a new-format element, it will treat 'p' as `KeyVer` and the remaining 8 bytes as the next element's flag stream, leading to decode failure (`invalid temp index value`) in `DecodeTempIndexValue`.
Readers that hard-fail on decode include `pkg/ddl/index_merge_tmp.go` (merge step calls `tablecodec.DecodeTempIndexValue(rawValue)` and returns the error) and DML paths like `pkg/table/tables/index.go` / `fetchDuplicatedHandleForTempIndexKey` (decode error bubbles up).
findings.fix: Gate emission of the new temp-index element encoding until the cluster is guaranteed homogeneous (e.g., via cluster/version capability in PD/meta, or by only enabling this format after a controlled version bump), otherwise continue emitting the old format during mixed-version windows. If gating is not feasible, document/guard that global-index temp-index merge (and DML that writes these temp values) must not run during rolling upgrade/downgrade.
findings.impact:
Mixed-version TiDB clusters (rolling upgrade/downgrade) with an in-flight ADD GLOBAL UNIQUE INDEX using temp-index can break when upgraded nodes write the new-format temp-index delete markers and older nodes attempt to read them:
- DDL merge-temp-index step can abort on decode error, potentially stalling/failing the DDL job.
- DML that touches the temp index (unique checks / conflict handling) can error.
This is a compatibility hazard for online upgrades if DDL is running/allowed during the upgrade window.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master`: `pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go` on `upstream/master` still contains the same `TempIndexKeyTypePartitionIDFlag` encode/decode branch for temp-index deleted+distinct elements.
findings.verify: Repro in mixed versions: start `ALTER TABLE ... ADD UNIQUE INDEX ... GLOBAL` (ingest/temp-index path) on a partitioned table, upgrade only one TiDB node to the new version, keep another node on the pre-#57017 version (preferably DDL owner), generate concurrent UPDATE/DELETE to produce temp-index delete markers, and observe old node failing to decode temp-index values (DDL merge fails or DML errors). Also validate that after full upgrade (all nodes new), the scenario passes and merge completes.
findings.what: TempIndexValue encoding change (global unique index delete marker adds 'p'+partitionID bytes) is not forward-compatible: pre-#57017 TiDB cannot decode new-format temp-index values, risking rolling upgrade/downgrade failures when temp-index is active.

subject: *: let TempIndex support encode/decode partitionID flag (#57017)
summary: Change correctly carries partition ID through temp-index delete markers for global unique indexes (via `TempIndexValueElem.Global` + `PartitionHandle`) and updates merge logic to interpret it. Main remaining risk is compatibility: the new temp-index value element format is not decodable by pre-#57017 nodes, which can break mixed-version rolling upgrade/downgrade if add-index temp-index is active.
